package com.example.payment.app;

import com.example.payment.application.AuthorizePayment;
import com.example.payment.application.PaymentGateway;
import com.example.payment.application.ReceiptStore;
import com.example.payment.infrastructure.FileSystemReceiptStore;
import com.example.payment.infrastructure.HttpPaymentGateway;
import java.nio.file.Path;
import org.springframework.beans.factory.annotation.Value;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.web.client.RestClient;

@Configuration
class PaymentConfiguration {

    @Bean
    PaymentGateway paymentGateway(RestClient.Builder builder, @Value("${payment.provider.base-url}") String baseUrl) {
        return new HttpPaymentGateway(builder.baseUrl(baseUrl).build());
    }

    @Bean
    ReceiptStore receiptStore(@Value("${payment.receipts.directory}") Path directory) {
        return new FileSystemReceiptStore(directory);
    }

    @Bean
    AuthorizePayment authorizePayment(PaymentGateway gateway, ReceiptStore receipts) {
        return new AuthorizePayment(gateway, receipts);
    }
}

Full build passes (7/7 tests). Summary of the fix:

- Added `wiremock-standalone` as a test dependency to `payment-integration-test`.
- Added `HttpPaymentGatewayTest`, which stubs the provider's HTTP API and drives `HttpPaymentGateway` end-to-end, verifying:
  - the outbound JSON (`reference`/`amount`/`currency`, currency uppercased) matches what the provider expects
  - a `200 {"status":"approved"}` response yields `APPROVED`
  - a `200 {"status":"declined"}` response yields `DECLINED`
  - a `402` refusal (no body) is treated as `DECLINED`
  - any other unexpected error status (`500`) is surfaced as an `IllegalStateException`
  - an unrecognized/ambiguous status value defaults safely to `DECLINED`
- Forced the test's `RestClient` to HTTP/1.1 (via `JdkClientHttpRequestFactory`) since WireMock's HTTP/2 support conflicted with the JDK client, causing spurious stream resets.
